## 債市主線

生產者物價漲幅低於預期，緩和市場對聯準會一次升息50個基點的疑慮，帶動短天期美國公債回升；長天期殖利率則小幅走高，為跌勢沉重的一週畫下句點。2年期殖利率下降3.95個基點至4.8419%，10年期上升0.81個基點至5.1352%。週五曲線轉陡，反映市場對下次升息幅度稍感寬慰，但持續的基礎通膨壓力，仍使進一步緊縮成為大方向。

10月整體生產者物價月增率明顯放緩，排除食品、能源與貿易服務後，月增率卻仍達0.5%。John Williams、Austan Goolsbee、Susan Collins與Philip Jefferson的新發言都支持進一步抑制需求，但對步調及就業風險各有側重。據Bloomberg報導，截至本週末，利率市場反映到2027年9月前約升息90個基點，一週前約為50個基點。

AI建設帶來的融資壓力也更為具體。QTS因投資人抗拒定價而縮減籌資規模，Nscale披露借款激增及龐大的後續資金需求，Natixis新研究則指出，資料中心貸款避險也是推升利率的來源。債券投資人須評估的影響，已延伸至科技股波動以外。美國投資級債利差當日大致持平，高收益債利差則小幅擴大。

## PPI降溫，聯準會仍須權衡升息步調

生產者物價數據為本週對政策加速收緊的憂慮帶來即時紓解。10月最終需求PPI月增0.3%，低於市場共識0.4%，也較9月修正後的1.4%大幅放緩。美國勞工統計局將9月漲幅由1.3%上修，遲報與資料更正同時影響6月至9月數據。年增率仍由6.3%升至6.5%，創2022年11月以來最高，惟略低於預期的6.6%。

商品與服務漲幅都放緩，但殘留壓力的來源不同。商品價格月增0.5%，低於9月的2.5%；其中，排除食品與能源的商品價格同樣上漲0.5%，貢獻10月商品漲幅逾60%。食品上漲1.3%，能源下降0.1%，商品價格年增率則為10.2%。整體漲幅回落，包含能源降價的影響，其他商品仍持續漲價。

服務價格上漲0.2%，連續第五個月走高。運輸與倉儲上漲2.0%，貢獻服務漲幅的四分之三；卡車貨運價格上升3.9%，對整體服務價格漲幅的貢獻超過80%。另一方面，貿易服務價差下降0.2%，機械與車輛批發價差下降4.2%，系統軟體及航空客運價格亦下跌。這些項目抵銷部分漲勢，使運費持續上揚之際，整體服務漲幅仍受控制。

不同基礎指標呈現的訊息不盡相同。核心PPI月增0.3%，符合共識，較修正後的0.8%放緩；核心年增率維持5.0%，也符合預期。排除食品、能源與貿易服務後，價格連續第二個月上升0.5%，高於Trading Economics預測的0.3%，年增率則由5.0%降至4.9%。生產鏈上游方面，加工中間財上漲0.4%，未加工商品下跌3.1%，中間服務上漲0.6%。

BMO Capital Markets的Vail Hartman認為，PPI中納入聯準會偏好通膨指標的分項，10月表現較弱。LPL Financial的Jeffrey Roach預期12月升息25個基點，認為一次升50個基點會帶來不必要的經濟風險。JPMorgan Asset Management的Priya Misra也認為，聯準會無須急於升息50個基點，並警告這可能讓投資人推斷中性利率大幅高於原先認知。這些看法說明，儘管生產者物價年增率仍在加速，較溫和的整體月增率仍足以影響政策預期。

美債買盤主要集中在短端。5年期殖利率下降0.88個基點至4.9616%，30年期則上升1.34個基點至5.4655%。2年與10年期利差擴大4.76個基點至29.33個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大5.29個基點至62.36個基點。市場降低對近期政策大幅調整的預期，對最受聯準會決策影響的年期支撐最明顯。

週五的回升並未扭轉本週大幅重新定價。相較11月6日，2年期殖利率仍上升33.04個基點，5年期上升31.67個基點，10年期上升27.78個基點，30年期上升20.1個基點。全週曲線仍趨平，2年與10年期利差縮小5.26個基點。以一個月比較，2年期殖利率上升5.29個基點，10年與30年期則分別仍低7.32與9.14個基點。

長天期殖利率的調整，主要仍來自實質殖利率。10年期抗通膨公債（TIPS）殖利率週五上升1.85個基點至2.8847%，損益兩平通膨率下降1.04個基點至2.2505%。全週實質殖利率上升27.2個基點，通膨補償僅增加0.58個基點。通膨消息與政策討論對實質借款成本的推升，遠大於對長期通膨補償的影響；評估企業籌資興建長期專案所承受的緊縮壓力時，這項區別尤其重要。

Williams於紐約時間週四晚間表示，通膨仍遠高於適當水準，要使其持續回到2%，還須採取進一步行動，同時應避免對充分就業造成過度傷害。他形容經濟成長與勞動市場正在增強，但不認為經濟已失衡。這番較居中的政策評估支持繼續緊縮，並未表態支持12月擴大升息幅度。

芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Goolsbee在週五CNBC訪談中，更強調抗通膨公信力。他表示物價壓力上升，持續時間超出官員預期，央行還有工作要做，才能重新建立抗通膨的信譽。Collins當天另表示，近期適合進一步緊縮；需求穩健之下，壓力已由能源擴及其他領域，但她未說明利率應上升多少或多快。

Collins也談到房市的取捨。她表示，利率升高，短期內可能增加購屋與建屋成本，但物價穩定能在較長時間提供更可預測的環境。在房市已經疲弱的情況下，她承認恢復物價穩定會使短期購屋負擔加重，未認為房市能輕鬆承受融資成本上升。

Jefferson為週五聖地牙哥演說準備的講稿指出，經濟活動與勞動情況穩健、物價壓力持續，因此決定政策立場時，應優先考量通膨走向。他並區分貨幣政策可影響的循環性失業，以及科技造成的勞工技能與雇主需求錯配。AI投資與生產力提升可能藉由支撐投資和消費，推高中性利率；不過，生產力與實質利率的歷史關聯雜訊很大，使這類變化難以預測。

政策討論在週五收盤後延續。今年沒有投票權的Collins週六表示，穩定、漸進的路徑似乎適當，但仍保持開放態度。她認為通膨預期約在2%，薪資漲勢集中於部分技術勞工。她的基本情境是消費與企業投資持續、政策略為收緊，而勞動市場損害有限；若薪資漲勢擴大、需求更強或再遭遇衝擊，通膨則可能更加持久。

堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid週日另提出評估。他引用聯準會偏好指標9月通膨率3.6%的數據，表示自8月以來，恢復物價穩定的任務變得更困難。能源、關稅相關耐久財成本、AI建設及醫療保健都在推升物價，不能逕自假設生產成本上升只是暫時現象。他認為經濟成長穩健、失業率低，但薪資與勞動市場目前並非重要的通膨來源；這與擔心招聘增強可能形成新壓力的看法有所不同。

政策路徑預測也分歧。美國銀行目前預期接下來三次會議都會升息，Santander則預測12月與3月升息。PGIM的Robert Sockin認為，在經濟強勁、通膨偏高的環境採取漸進步調，可能使日後不得不更快、更多地緊縮。9月升息、10月暫停後，目標區間維持3.75%至4%；各方爭論的是此後緊縮的時點與總幅度。

## AI融資面臨價格與承接能力限制

QTS最新一筆大型融資，直接反映投資人對價格與曝險的限制。這家由Blackstone支持的資料中心營運商，原擬籌資約$8億，但部分投資人不接受定價，另一些在公司多次發債後已面臨曝險限制，最終規模降至約$3億。Blackstone選擇按希望的條件縮小交易，因為若利差大幅放寬，可能成為其他相關借款人更昂貴的定價參考。

其中，$1億、7年期美國私募債已於週五定價，較基準利率高2.45個百分點；另$2億、5年期銀行貸款預期未來幾週定價。原本$8億私募債的用途，是償還既有5年期銀行債務；發行規模縮小後，該筆既有融資可以繼續保留。

QTS反覆向相對有限的投資人群籌資，加重了承接限制。過去18個月，公司至少透過兩筆私募債籌得數十億美元，包括去年$16.5億及另一筆$8億融資。據Private Placement Monitor，投資級真正私募債市場去年發行量僅略高於$2,000億，重要買家包括壽險公司與長期資產管理機構。QTS另於4月與8月透過專案融資綠色債券，分別借入$46億與$39億。因此，投資人還能增加多少曝險、以及要求什麼價格，成為這次交易的關鍵。

Nscale修訂後的IPO申報文件，顯示資產負債表急速擴張，建設時程所需資金也更為吃緊。債務由6月底的$1.374億，升至9月30日的$55億。9月議定、總額逾$30億的可轉換融資中，Nvidia承諾提供$20億，是先前披露$10億的兩倍。Nvidia同時是主要股東與設備供應商，但沒有義務優先配貨、提供優惠價格或讓Nscale提早取得產品。

營運規模正在增加。Nscale約$1,060億合約總值中，已投入營運的部分約$64億，高於8月底的$26億，新增部分多來自Microsoft出資的德州設施。不過，最大客戶合約仍須大量融資支持：與Anthropic簽訂的6年期、$446億合約涵蓋460百萬瓦容量，預定2027年末段開始陸續上線。Nscale已承諾為西維吉尼亞州Monarch開發案投入約$10億，要完成專案，至少還需$300億。

若未取得融資或交付延誤，Anthropic可以終止合約；雙方也正洽談Monarch第二棟建築。Nscale表示，近期預估資本承諾顯著增加，主要用於設備，屆時未必能按可接受條件取得額外資金。另一筆與機器人開發商Figure AI約$35億的合約，將以一半現金、一半股權支付，條件取決於Figure估值。不同客戶合約因此有各自的資金需求與對價形式。

Natixis的John Briggs與Eric Benoist新研究，指出這些融資活動透過避險傳導至利率市場。資料中心開發商通常以長期超大規模雲端業者租約為基礎，借入浮動利率貸款，再透過利率交換支付固定利率，以穩定借款成本。Natixis估計，這類貸款避險於2026年增加的DV01為$3.17億，超過直接發債所帶來的$2.1億。

兩者合計，AI債券與資料中心貸款對利率每變動1個基點的敏感金額約為$5.3億。Natixis估計，這項額外利率風險負擔，貢獻了今年美債殖利率漲幅中的約45個基點。借款人在交換市場支付固定利率，也使交換利差高於依一級交易商美債部位歷史關係所推估的水準。這是研究對年初至今影響的估算，指出貸款避險除了傳統發債排擠效應外，還提供另一條傳導管道。

Natixis預測，2027年合計曝險可能達$7.5億，相較之下，美國財政部每年發行10年期及更長年期債務帶來的利率敏感金額約$9.5億。該預測以AI借款持續為前提，因此Nvidia領導層過渡後，專案推進與融資情況若有變化，也會影響結果。

JPMorgan週五的供給展望，呈現公開債券市場潛在發行規模。Nathaniel Rosenbaum等策略師預測，明年美國高評級債發行量達$2.1兆，高於其對2026年的$2兆估計。科技與媒體業預計占$6,120億、接近總量30%，包括超大規模雲端業者$2,250億，以及資料中心與運算晶片融資另$2,250億。

即使JPMorgan預期併購相關發債減少52%，整體預測仍高度依賴AI資本支出循環。若交易活動更強，供給可能增加；若轉向外幣融資，或原訂2028年的專案受許可及開發延誤影響，美元發債則可能減少。TD Securities預估明年發行$2.4兆，美國銀行則考量融資管道多元化及併購降溫，預測$1.9兆。已宣布的投資究竟有多少會進入這個市場，各方仍有很大歧見。

整體市場波動之際，公司債需求仍具韌性。Bloomberg高評級債總報酬指數自9月底至週五上漲1.2%，同期標普500含股息下跌約1.1%。週五公司債平均殖利率為6%，平均利差86個基點，最近一週收窄5個基點；週五整體投資級債利差則大致持平。基準殖利率上升仍拖累當日報酬，LQD含配息下跌0.23%，HYG下跌0.05%。

聯準會週五《金融穩定報告》將這些融資發展，置於更廣泛的脆弱性評估中。報告指出資產估值偏高，並關注資本支出與債務發行。受訪者提及AI降低網路攻擊難度、風險資產修正、長期利率上升與財政可持續性等風險。這是脆弱性檢視，並非預測上述事件將會發生。

週末另有Firmus籌資提案的報導。《澳洲金融評論》指出，這家資料中心開發商上月放棄IPO後，擬透過股權、債務與客戶預付款，私下籌集$30億。與Nvidia、Meta等客戶洽談預付款的進度最深入，可能使合約金額的12.5%提前支付。先前上市計畫連同超額配售選擇權，原擬籌集最多$55億，但需求不足；新方案將轉向其他途徑尋求擴張資金。

## 各國貨幣政策路徑分歧

日本債市同時承受美國利率再度上升，以及國內緊縮預期增強的壓力。週五10年期日本公債殖利率上升8個基點至2.87%，30年期上升7個基點至3.99%。隔夜指數交換反映，日本央行到12月前升息的機率約87%，高於前一週約50%的低點。東海東京證券的佐野一彥認為，賣壓可能過頭，但眼前缺乏足以支撐持續回升的催化因素。

澳洲公債的相對定價朝另一方向移動。週五雪梨早盤，10年期殖利率較同年期美債低2個基點；若維持到收盤，將是2025年8月以來首次收在美債下方。市場預期澳洲央行緊縮接近尾聲，與聯準會可能拉長升息循環形成差異。FIIG的Philip Brown認為，澳洲定價反映經濟將受損、2027年底將降息的預期。澳洲聯邦銀行的Michael Tang預估，明年澳債與美債利差可維持負10至負15個基點，但提醒澳洲曲線估值偏貴，可能放慢短期需求。

歐洲數據再度顯示經濟韌性。歐盟統計局第二次估計顯示，第三季GDP成長0.4%，與初值相同。伊朗戰爭推升能源價格後，即使借款成本已上調兩次，歐元區經濟仍持續擴張。通膨約為2%目標的兩倍，成長韌性讓官員有空間考慮12月再升息，儘管歐洲央行認為成長風險偏下行、通膨風險偏上行。

德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel週五演說提出更鮮明的通膨警訊。他表示，能源價格已大幅高於9月假設路徑，使情況更接近預測中的不利情境。天然氣與電價動能增強、上游成本上升，短期預期也隨整體通膨走高。若情況持續，極可能需要進一步行動；高通膨每多維持一個月，第二輪效應風險就更高。

歐洲央行接班磋商也有了更緊迫的時程。德國總理Friedrich Merz週五表示，德國將在未來一週提出三個執行理事會職缺的一攬子人選，密集討論仍在進行，尚未達成協議。Isabel Schnabel與Philip Lane現任職位的候選人，須在11月18日前提出，以趕上11月26日至27日領袖峰會前的推薦程序。Schnabel將於1月卸任，Christine Lagarde於2月、Lane於5月離任。

與Pablo Hernandez de Cos競逐總裁職位的Klaas Knot，週日在《晚郵報》訪談中，說明對主權市場支持與通膨的立場。他認為歐洲央行干預可以保護市場免受失序影響，但健全財政仍是各國政府的責任。國內需求、就業與民間資產負債表的韌性，加上國防支出及美國AI投資的外溢效應，都支撐經濟活動。

Knot對通膨的評估較為審慎：預期仍受錨定，廣泛第二輪效應的證據有限。關鍵在於能源壓力是否傳入薪資及更廣泛物價，中東情勢具有決定性。各國政府評估接班人選之際，未來政策制定者可能須同時處理通膨與再起的主權市場動盪，他的立場因此受到關注。

秘魯週四已實際升息25個基點，將基準利率調至4.50%，為近四年首次升息。受訪分析師多數預期此舉，13人中僅兩人預期維持不變。食品與能源成本上升，使10月通膨達5.25%，為2023年以來最快，且連續第八個月超過3%的目標上限。

秘魯央行預期，隨供給衝擊消退，整體與核心通膨將回到接近2%，但警告聖嬰現象及中東緊張可能使衝擊延續。央行明確保留下一次決策的彈性，未承諾連續升息。總裁Julio Velarde於9月將2026年通膨預測由3.8%上修至4.2%，預估2027年回到目標區間。

墨西哥意外降息後，其政策分歧持續受到檢視，新報導凸顯各方對降息目的的不同解讀。美國銀行的Carlos Capistran表示，投資人質疑決策是否受到藉披索貶值支持成長，或降低政府融資成本的考量影響。央行總裁Victoria Rodríguez否認鎖定特定匯率水準，並形容披索大幅升值後的近期調整有序。披索自9月初高點下跌近9%，至每美元約18.60披索，美國銀行預期明年達19。這些具名解讀之外，10月通膨為3.75%，墨西哥央行也已示意不急於再次降息。

## 債務協商與財報牽動個別借款人定價

塞內加爾預算僵局的負面影響，蓋過債務核實取得的進展。2031年到期美元債殖利率全週上升109個基點，升至9月以來最高，2033年期殖利率上升75個基點。政府與IMF初步達成$22億協議，但作為基礎的2026年修正預算及2027年支出計畫，仍須國會批准。Ousmane Sonko所屬、掌握多數席次的Pastef黨議員，反對部分調整，尤其削減公共投資；Sonko也質疑債務重整條件。

週五報導披露，政府已於上月委任Deloitte，推進了IMF董事會審議前的一項必要程序。先前Forvis Mazars核對帳目後，2023年底中央政府債務占GDP比率由約74%上修至111%；IMF估計2024年底債務占比則為132%。這些不同時點的債務估計，顯示新一輪稽核須處理的帳目問題規模龐大。

IMF發言人Julie Kozack週四表示，預算須符合雙方議定政策，並能在塞內加爾法律及憲政架構下落實。債務誤報的矯正措施與融資保證也不可或缺。包括中國與法國在內的官方債權人委員會尚未成立。塞內加爾目標在12月前與官方債權人及債券持有人達成原則性協議；Lazard與Global Sovereign Advisory為該國提供顧問服務，Alvarez & Marsal與White & Case則代表一個債券持有人團體。

委內瑞拉的多邊融資則循另一條路徑推進。美洲開發銀行（IDB）董事會週五同意，透過涵蓋技術援助、民間部門支持及潛在投資的架構，恢復往來。另據知情人士，美國財政部正考慮一項隔夜過橋安排，用以清償委內瑞拉積欠IDB約$23億的款項；擬議資金將付給IDB，而非直接交給委內瑞拉。

欠款若清償，IDB可在2018年暫停放款後恢復貸款，委內瑞拉也可向其他多邊機構提出申請。IDB未來兩年潛在貸款可達$60億，世界銀行則表示同期最多可貸$50億。參議員Elizabeth Warren先前反對以財政部外匯平準基金，為投資委內瑞拉的金融公司提供保證，因此這項擬議融資途徑仍面臨國會檢視。

巴西CSN財報引發即時且劇烈的重新定價。據Bloomberg引述TRACE資料，週五紐約時間上午11時06分，CSN的2031年期美元債每1美元面額下跌3.38美分至48美分；股價盤中一度下跌12%，觸及2016年以來低點。第三季調整後淨利由去年同期獲利7,600萬巴西雷亞爾，轉為虧損12.5億雷亞爾；EBITDA下降43%至18.8億雷亞爾，低於分析師預估的19.4億雷亞爾。

成本增加、鐵礦砂價格下降、海外鋼鐵銷售疲弱及水泥生產支出，均拖累業績。淨負債達449億雷亞爾，淨負債對調整後EBITDA比率升至4.23倍。執行長Fabio Schvartsman表示，完成尚待交割的資產出售後，將尋求銀行降低利率並延長到期日。已議定出售的資產，包括作價127億雷亞爾的水泥事業，以及企業價值約€5.5億的德國鋼鐵事業。

CSN仍優先推動預定2028年的P15鐵礦砂擴產案。施工正推高當前資本支出，公司預期最終可每年增加1,650萬噸高品位產量，以及逾40億雷亞爾的長期扣除特定項目前獲利。這些效益尚在未來，當前現金創造能力與資產出售能否落實，仍是降低槓桿的關鍵。

馬來西亞Zetrix AI除逾期付款外，也面臨債券契約問題。創辦人Wong Thean Soon為因應追繳保證金，6月至10月出售22.2億股，失去最大股東身分，使公司可能違反要求他維持該身分的伊斯蘭債券條款。MARC將債務評級降至僅較違約高一級，Zetrix並披露，11月6日應付的2,500萬令吉債券款項仍未支付。

當局指公司積欠3.14億令吉政府費用後，其僅存的道路通行費代收服務也遭暫停。Wong表示，公司轉向AI、區塊鏈及國際業務之際，首要任務是履行義務並強化營運。公司原有政府服務業務已大幅流失，市值也由105億令吉高峰降至約4.3億令吉。

併購融資市場另出現新的次級價格警訊。Intersnack以$29億收購Utz的一筆逾$10億貸款，在交易預期完成前，本週報價已降至每1美元面額約88美分，9月定價時為99美分。發行後不久即大幅下跌，為當日廣泛高收益債利差僅溫和擴大的背景，增添一項個別借款人的價格訊號。

## 供給稀缺與本地融資改變資金配置

新興市場主權債發行急遽萎縮，近期交易卻仍吸引大量訂單。Bloomberg週末分析指出，下半年硬通貨債券發行額為$690億，較去年同期減少41%，9月以來發行量約減半。Pictet的Reza Karim認為，美國利率波動與地緣政治風險，使可行發行窗口不足；Promeritum的Chris Celio也表示，市場震盪讓發行人難以有把握地建立訂單。

發行窗口有限，近期交易仍獲踴躍認購。William Blair的Yvette Babb指出，秘魯發債訂單約為發行額五倍，Ecopetrol約三倍；印尼一筆伊斯蘭債券也獲三倍認購，定價較初步指引收窄25至30個基點。羅馬尼亞€45億交易吸引逾€76億訂單。Celio表示，找不到新券可買的現金，可能流向既有債券，支撐次級市場價格。

Bloomberg比較顯示，這類資產今年下跌0.5%，美國公債與美國公司債則分別下跌1.5%與1.8%。TT International的Jean-Charles Sambor預期，新興市場債相對美國高收益債將持續領先，理由是供需技術面更強、供給風險較低及基本面改善。Karim預期2027年初發債可能大幅回升，因此目前供給稀缺的支撐能維持多久，取決於融資窗口何時重新開啟。

印度最大退休金管理機構則正為各邦債務供給增加作準備。管理約$640億資產的SBI Pension Fund，計畫在1月至3月各邦借款上升之際，增購邦債。投資長Sandeep Pandey預期，邦債相對中央政府債的殖利率溢酬將再度擴大。目前10年期溢酬約60個基點，4月一度達90個基點，創近五年高點。

截至10月底，邦債約占SBI持有部位17%。這家機構過去18個月縮短存續期間，近期增加現金，並著重邦債與最高評級公司債的利息收益。在中央政府借款量也很大的情況下，其配置計畫顯示不同公共借款人之間的競爭，如何改變機構資金流向。

中國政策性銀行債市則遭遇更即時的配置衝擊。國家開發銀行10年期殖利率週四上升3個基點，追平今年最大單日升幅；相對同年期國債溢酬擴大至約9個基點，為逾六個月最高。中國進出口銀行與中國農業發展銀行債券殖利率也上升。

市場擔心可能對國債利息收入課稅，推高國債殖利率，迫使其他債券重新定價。華創將政策性銀行債賣壓歸因於這項疑慮；天風表示，若國債殖利率提高、削弱政策性銀行債的相對吸引力，共同基金可能重新考慮配置。稅案仍在研議，但價格調整已由諮詢直接涉及的國債，延伸至其他債券。

越南貸款成長快於存款，銀行正以存款利率吸引家庭資金離開股市。央行於10月底要求降息前，存款利率已連續上升11個月。部分銀行臨櫃利率仍高達7%，Bloomberg受訪客戶主要在中小型銀行，取得超過9%的議價利率。Kenno Asset Management的Chris Hunt指出，流動性吃緊與貸款需求強勁，推動銀行競相攬存。

資金重配已反映在證券帳戶。第三季末帳戶現金年減49%至64.9兆越南盾，為2024年第四季以來最低；10月股票成交額降至2020年8月以來最低單月水準。8月底家庭存款達11,430兆越南盾，外資今年淨賣出股票$46億，接近2025年全年$48億的紀錄。即使市場准入改革已使越南獲富時羅素升級為新興市場，銀行高融資利率仍在改變本地資產需求。

辛巴威則希望建立更長的本幣殖利率曲線。央行總裁John Mushayavanhu表示，計畫在現有30天與90天工具以外，延長ZiG定期存款工具年期，預期政府債券也會隨之推出。9月工具殖利率分別為8%與11%，均全額認購；目標是讓ZiG除交易用途外，也能成為儲值工具。

這項規劃之前，央行已大力支撐匯率。2026年前九個月，央行投入$13.5億干預，ZiG仍貶值近3%。Mushayavanhu表示，超過$20億的準備資產足以支應流通中的ZiG320億，據此換算約每美元18 ZiG，相較週四市場匯率26.43。他對本幣低估的判斷伴隨市場發展計畫提出，其中準備資產與流通貨幣的比較，是總裁本人的計算。

週五Microsoft服務中斷，另對市場作業造成獨立干擾，延誤通訊與交易處理。新加坡交易員表示部分融資交易無法完成，歐洲交易所遭遇電子郵件問題，日本交易室改用電話與傳真。BNP Paribas Asset Management的Ryutaro Kimura表示，交易大致持續進行，但確認作業積壓，造成交割問題。Kyte Broking的Andy Kent預期，直通式處理恢復前，交易意願將下降。Microsoft於美國交易時段表示，服務恢復已有進展。

達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan週五另提議，區分為維持市場運作而買入的證券，以及為貨幣政策持有的資產。她認為，另設帳戶並承諾迅速出售干預資產，可減少非預期刺激。評估美債市場運作時，她觀察買賣價差、深度與價格衝擊，不會僅因殖利率快速上升就認定須干預。她也呼籲機構預先備妥緊急流動性管道，並讓指定金融市場基礎設施，在週末、假日等異常情況可使用貼現窗口。

## 後續市場焦點

接下來的美國數據，將檢驗需求能承受多少實質借款成本上升。11月紐約州製造業指數於11月16日公布，Trading Economics預測由25.5降至10。11月17日每週ADP就業數據前值為19,750人；10月零售銷售預測月增0.6%，前值0.8%。進口物價預測月增1.7%，前值1.1%；出口物價預測月增1.4%，前值2.2%，將分別提供境外成本傳導的新訊息。

聯準會10月會議紀錄，以及主席Kevin Warsh、Williams與Neel Kashkari即將發表的談話，將有助區分官員支持連續每次升息25個基點，或認為有必要加大單次幅度。該次會議在強勁的10月非農就業與CPI報告前舉行，當時兩名官員異議支持緊縮。Warsh週一活動聚焦AI與生產力，與Jefferson對中性利率的不確定性相關，不過Warsh一直避免提供近期政策指引。美國財政部即將標售20年期公債與10年期抗通膨公債，也將在本週賣壓後檢驗利率風險承接需求。

11月19日初領失業救濟人數預測為19.4萬人，前值20萬人；續領預測為172.5萬人，前值169.7萬人。費城聯準銀行製造業指數預測由20.9降至19。利率爭論愈來愈聚焦成長與通膨能否同時持續，這些數據將補充企業留用員工及工業活動的最新情況。

中國週一活動數據，將是9月底支持措施後首次全面觀察。經濟學家預期工業生產年增5.3%，零售銷售年增0.8%，低於9月1.1%；1月至10月固定資產投資預期下降1.7%。截至10月28日，人民幣8,000億元政策性銀行融資已投放，地方政府另獲人民幣2,500億元專項債額度，用於年底前投資。12月經濟政策會議前，這些數據將顯示融資有多少已轉化為實際活動。

日本第三季GDP年化成長率預測由1.4%放緩至0.2%，民間消費可能萎縮；本週稍後公布的10月CPI，預期進一步高於日本央行2%目標。這些數據直接關係到再度升溫的緊縮預期，是否與國內需求相容。澳洲薪資、就業數據及澳洲央行會議紀錄，則將檢驗澳美公債已呈現的相對利率分歧。

英國成長具韌性之後，週二勞動數據與週三CPI尤其重要。整體通膨預測為3.6%，由燃料與家庭能源成本帶動。失業率預測有所差異：Bloomberg Economics預測截至9月的三個月為4.6%，另一份下週整體展望則預期4.7%。英國央行對能源壓力是否擴散的判斷，將影響12月可能升息的決策。加拿大週一公布通膨，整體年增率預測3.2%，核心指標接近2%；印尼央行週三決策，初步預測是在印尼盾承壓下升息25個基點。

Nvidia股價全週下跌13%後，11月17日財報將成為臨時領導層上任後，首次重要營運檢驗。公司是否有能力、也願意繼續為客戶提供融資，與Nscale資金需求及更廣泛的晶片支持借款有關。週末報導再提領導層改組壓力，並稱曾討論Huang可能回任；公司此前則表示仍在挑選獵才公司。Anthropic即將進行首次公開募股，將另行檢驗強勁訂單能否轉化為資金。交易商預期未來一週美國債券銷售約$350億，歐洲調查所有受訪者均預期發行至少相當於€300億。

塞內加爾預算批准、融資保證與債權人協商，仍決定IMF董事會審議能否推進。委內瑞拉擬議過橋融資則須先議定清償欠款機制，才可展開新的多邊貸款。最新人事委任或董事會架構，尚未解決各自的時程問題。

週末局勢升級，使能源安全仍是獨立的不確定來源。伊朗軍方表示向巴林一處空軍基地發射六架無人機，是9月初以來首次此類攻擊，同時重申仍有結束戰爭的途徑。此前，國際能源署（IEA）週五預測季度石油供給將出現戰爭開始以來首次過剩。週五WTI期貨收於$88.56、下跌0.20%，布蘭特收於$95.84、上漲0.02%；週末攻擊的市場影響，仍待恢復交易後觀察。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Short-dated Treasuries recovered as softer-than-expected producer inflation eased concern about a half-point Federal Reserve increase, while longer yields edged higher to end a bruising week. The two-year yield fell 3.95 basis points to 4.8419%; the 10-year rose 0.81 basis point to 5.1352%. Friday's steepening reflected some relief over the size of the next policy move, with persistent underlying price pressure keeping the broader tightening cycle in view.

October's headline producer-price increase slowed sharply, but the measure excluding food, energy and trade services continued to rise 0.5% monthly. Fresh remarks from John Williams, Austan Goolsbee, Susan Collins and Philip Jefferson reinforced the case for further restraint while preserving important differences over its pace and the risks to employment. By the end of the week, rates markets were pricing around 90 basis points of tightening by September 2027, against roughly 50 basis points a week earlier, according to Bloomberg.

The financing consequences of the AI buildout became more concrete. QTS reduced a planned debt raising after resistance to pricing, Nscale disclosed a steep increase in borrowing and substantial additional funding requirements, and new Natixis research identified data-center loan hedging as another source of upward pressure on rates. Those developments gave bond investors more to assess than technology-share volatility alone. U.S. investment-grade spreads were little changed on the day, while high-yield spreads widened modestly.

## PPI Relief Leaves the Fed Debating Pace

The producer-price release offered immediate relief from the week's more aggressive policy fears. Final-demand PPI rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% consensus and down from September's revised 1.4%. The Bureau of Labor Statistics revised the September increase from 1.3%, with late reports and corrections affecting June through September. Annual inflation nevertheless accelerated to 6.5% from 6.3%, its highest since November 2022, though slightly below the expected 6.6%.

Both goods and services inflation slowed, with distinctly different sources of remaining pressure. Goods prices rose 0.5%, against 2.5% in September. More than 60% of October's increase came from goods excluding food and energy, which also advanced 0.5%. Food rose 1.3%, while energy slipped 0.1%; goods prices were 10.2% above a year earlier. The headline moderation therefore included cheaper energy alongside continued increases across other products.

Services prices rose 0.2%, their fifth consecutive increase. Transportation and warehousing advanced 2.0% and accounted for three-quarters of the services gain. Truck freight prices rose 3.9%, contributing more than 80% of the overall services increase, while trade margins fell 0.2%. Machinery and vehicle wholesale margins dropped 4.2%; system software and airline passenger prices also declined. These offsets helped contain the aggregate even as freight costs continued to rise.

Underlying measures supplied different readings of that mix. Core PPI rose 0.3% monthly, matching consensus and slowing from a revised 0.8%, while annual core inflation held at 5.0%, also as expected. Excluding food, energy and trade services, prices increased 0.5% for a second month, above Trading Economics' 0.3% forecast, and rose 4.9% annually after 5.0%. Further back in the production chain, processed intermediate goods increased 0.4%, unprocessed goods fell 3.1% and intermediate services rose 0.6%.

BMO Capital Markets' Vail Hartman judged the PPI components feeding into the Fed's preferred inflation gauge weaker in October. LPL Financial's Jeffrey Roach expected a 25-basis-point December increase and argued that a 50-basis-point step would pose unnecessary economic risks. JPMorgan Asset Management's Priya Misra likewise saw no urgency for a half-point move and warned that it could prompt investors to infer a substantially higher neutral rate. Their assessments helped explain why the softer headline mattered even with annual producer inflation still accelerating.

The Treasury response was concentrated toward the front. Five-year yields declined 0.88 basis point to 4.9616%, while the 30-year rose 1.34 basis points to 5.4655%. The two- to 10-year spread widened 4.76 basis points to 29.33 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap increased 5.29 basis points to 62.36. A smaller expected near-term policy shock offered the most support to maturities closest to the Fed's decisions.

Friday's recovery left a large weekly repricing intact. Two-year yields finished 33.04 basis points above November 6, five-year yields 31.67 basis points higher, and 10-year yields up 27.78 basis points. The 30-year increase was 20.1 basis points. The curve consequently remained flatter over the week, with two- to 10-year steepness down 5.26 basis points. Over a month, the two-year yield was up 5.29 basis points, while the 10-year was still 7.32 basis points lower and the 30-year 9.14 basis points lower.

Real yields continued to account for most of the longer-maturity adjustment. The 10-year TIPS yield rose 1.85 basis points Friday to 2.8847%, while the breakeven declined 1.04 basis points to 2.2505%. Over the week, the real yield increased 27.2 basis points and inflation compensation just 0.58 basis point. The inflation news and policy debate were raising the real cost of borrowing much more than long-term inflation compensation. That distinction is important when evaluating the restraint facing companies financing long-lived projects.

Williams supplied a fresh policy assessment Thursday evening in New York. He said inflation remained far too high and further action would be needed to return it sustainably to 2%, while emphasizing the need to avoid undue harm to maximum employment. He described growth and the labor market as strengthening, but did not see an economy out of balance. His remarks added a centrist voice to the tightening case without endorsing a larger December step.

Goolsbee's Friday CNBC interview put greater emphasis on credibility. The Chicago Fed president said price pressure was rising and had proved more persistent than officials expected, leaving the central bank with further work to reestablish its inflation-fighting credibility. Collins, speaking separately Friday, said additional tightening would be appropriate soon and that pressure had broadened beyond energy amid healthy demand. She declined to specify how far or how fast rates should rise.

Collins also addressed the trade-off in housing. Higher rates can make homes more expensive to buy and build in the near term, she said, while stable prices create more predictable conditions over time. The distinction matters with housing already weak: her argument accepted a near-term affordability cost as part of restoring price stability, rather than suggesting the sector was weathering higher financing costs comfortably.

Jefferson, in Friday remarks prepared for a San Diego speech, gave the inflation trajectory priority in deciding the stance of policy because activity and labor conditions were solid while price pressure persisted. He also distinguished cyclical unemployment, which monetary policy can influence, from a technology-driven mismatch between workers' skills and employers' needs. AI investment and productivity could lift the neutral interest rate by supporting investment and consumption, he said, though the historically noisy link between productivity and real rates makes such shifts difficult to predict.

The debate continued after Friday's close. On Saturday, Collins, a nonvoter this year, said a steady, gradual path seemed appropriate while remaining open-minded. She saw inflation expectations around 2% and wage increases concentrated in skilled-worker pockets. Her central scenario combined continued consumption and business investment with somewhat tighter policy and limited labor-market damage; she also identified broader wage gains, stronger demand or additional shocks as routes to greater inflation persistence.

Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid added a separate Sunday assessment. He cited September inflation of 3.6% in the Fed's preferred gauge and said the task of restoring price stability had become harder since August. Energy, tariff-related durable-goods costs, AI construction and healthcare were contributing, he said, and higher production costs should not automatically be assumed temporary. He considered growth solid and unemployment low, while judging wages and the labor market not to be meaningful current inflation contributors. His emphasis differed from concerns that strengthening hiring might become a new source of pressure.

Forecasts of the policy sequence also diverged. Bank of America now expects increases at the next three meetings; Santander projects December and March. PGIM's Robert Sockin argued that gradualism risks requiring faster and greater eventual tightening in a strong, inflationary economy. These disagreements concern the timing and total extent of restraint after September's increase and October's pause left the target range at 3.75%-4%.

## AI Borrowing Encounters Price and Capacity Limits

QTS provided a direct example of investor resistance to another large financing. The Blackstone-backed data-center operator cut a planned raising to about $300 million from roughly $800 million after some investors resisted pricing and others faced exposure constraints following repeated offerings. Blackstone chose a smaller transaction at its desired terms because a substantially wider spread could become a more expensive reference for other related borrowers.

The package separates completed pricing from prospective funding. A $100 million seven-year U.S. private placement priced Friday at 2.45 percentage points over benchmarks. A $200 million five-year bank-loan portion is expected to price in the coming weeks. The original $800 million private placement was intended to refinance existing five-year bank debt; with the smaller deal, that financing can remain outstanding.

Repeated use of a relatively small investor pool contributed to the constraint. QTS had already raised billions through at least two private debt sales over the past 18 months, including $1.65 billion last year and another $800 million financing. The investment-grade true private-placement market issued just over $200 billion last year, according to Private Placement Monitor, with life insurers and long-term asset managers important buyers. QTS also borrowed $4.6 billion and $3.9 billion through project-finance green bonds in April and August. Investors' capacity for another exposure and the price demanded for it were therefore central to the latest transaction.

Nscale's amended IPO filing disclosed a much larger balance sheet and a more demanding construction timetable. Debt reached $5.5 billion on September 30 from $137.4 million at the end of June. Nvidia's commitment to the more than $3 billion convertible financing agreed in September was $2 billion, double the previously disclosed $1 billion. Nvidia is also a major shareholder and equipment supplier, but has no obligation to provide priority allocation, favorable pricing or early product access.

Operational capacity has expanded: about $6.4 billion of Nscale's roughly $106 billion total contract value is now operational, against $2.6 billion at the end of August, with much of the addition coming from a Microsoft-funded Texas facility. The largest customer commitment still requires substantial financing. A six-year, $44.6 billion Anthropic contract covers 460 megawatts scheduled to begin coming online in late 2027. Nscale has committed about $1 billion toward the Monarch, West Virginia, development and needs at least $30 billion more to complete it.

Anthropic can terminate if financing is not secured or the project is late. The companies are also negotiating a second building at Monarch. Nscale said near-term forecast capital commitments had risen significantly, principally for equipment, and additional funding might not be available when needed on acceptable terms. Another approximately $3.5 billion contract, with robotics developer Figure AI, would be paid half in cash and half in equity, with those terms dependent on Figure's valuation. Customer contracts thus bring different funding requirements and forms of consideration.

New research by Natixis' John Briggs and Eric Benoist connected this financing activity to interest-rate markets through hedging. Data-center developers commonly borrow at floating rates against long-term hyperscaler leases, then pay fixed rates through swaps to stabilize borrowing costs. Natixis estimates that this loan-related hedging added $317 million of DV01 in 2026, exceeding the $210 million associated with direct bond issuance.

Their combined estimate is about $530 million of sensitivity to a 1-basis-point rate move from AI bonds and data-center loans. Natixis attributes roughly 45 basis points of this year's increase in Treasury yields to that additional duration burden. Fixed-rate paying by borrowers has also kept swap spreads higher than primary-dealer Treasury positions would historically suggest. This is a research estimate of a year-to-date influence, with loan hedging supplying a channel beyond conventional bond-market crowding out.

Natixis projects that the combined exposure could reach $750 million in 2027, compared with about $950 million of annual duration issuance by Treasury at maturities of 10 years and beyond. That projection depends on continued AI borrowing, leaving it sensitive to changes in project execution and financing after Nvidia's leadership transition.

JPMorgan's Friday supply outlook shows the scale of the potential public-bond pipeline. Strategists including Nathaniel Rosenbaum forecast $2.1 trillion of U.S. high-grade issuance next year, against their $2 trillion estimate for 2026. Technology and media account for a projected $612 billion, nearly 30% of the total, including $225 billion from hyperscalers and another $225 billion from data-center and computing-chip financing.

The forecast depends heavily on the AI capital-spending cycle even as JPMorgan expects acquisition-related issuance to fall 52%. Stronger dealmaking could lift supply, while foreign-currency funding and permitting or development delays affecting 2028 projects could reduce dollar issuance. TD Securities expects $2.4 trillion next year; Bank of America forecasts $1.9 trillion as funding diversifies and acquisition activity cools. The range captures substantial disagreement over how much announced investment will reach this particular market.

Demand for corporate bonds has held up across the wider volatility. Bloomberg's high-grade total-return index gained 1.2% from the end of September through Friday, while the S&P 500 lost about 1.1% including dividends. Corporate yields averaged 6% Friday. Spreads averaged 86 basis points and had narrowed 5 basis points over the latest week, though Friday's broad investment-grade direction was little changed. Rising benchmark yields still weighed on daily returns: LQD lost 0.23% including distributions, compared with a 0.05% loss for HYG.

The Fed's Friday Financial Stability Report placed these financing developments within a broader vulnerability assessment. It described elevated asset valuations alongside concern about capital expenditure and debt issuance. Survey respondents flagged cyberattacks made easier by AI, risk-asset corrections, higher long-term rates and fiscal sustainability. The report is a review of vulnerabilities rather than a forecast of those events.

Weekend reporting brought a new funding proposal from Firmus. The Australian Financial Review said the data-center developer plans a $3 billion private raising through equity, debt and customer prepayments after abandoning its IPO last month. Talks over prepayments from customers including Nvidia and Meta were the most advanced and could result in 12.5% of contracts being paid upfront. The proposal would redirect the search for expansion capital after insufficient demand for a listing that had sought up to $5.5 billion including an overallotment option.

## Global Policy Paths Separate

Japan's bond market absorbed the renewed pressure from U.S. rates alongside stronger domestic tightening expectations. On Friday, the 10-year JGB yield rose 8 basis points to 2.87%, and the 30-year increased 7 basis points to 3.99%. Overnight-indexed swaps implied about an 87% chance of a BOJ increase by December, up from a low near 50% the preceding week. Tokai Tokyo Securities' Kazuhiko Sano thought the selloff could have overshot but saw few immediate catalysts for a sustained recovery.

Australia's relative pricing moved in a different direction. Its 10-year yield fell 2 basis points below the U.S. equivalent in early Sydney trading Friday, a gap that would mark the first negative close since August 2025 if sustained. Expectations that the RBA is nearing the end of tightening contrast with a more extended Fed cycle. FIIG's Philip Brown attributed Australian pricing to expectations of economic damage and cuts late in 2027; Commonwealth Bank's Michael Tang envisaged a negative spread of 10-15 basis points through next year, while cautioning that a rich Australian curve could slow near-term demand.

European data gave the ECB a fresh confirmation of resilience. Eurostat's second estimate showed Q3 GDP rising 0.4%, unchanged from the initial reading. The bloc has continued to expand after two increases in borrowing costs since the Iran war lifted energy prices. With inflation around twice the 2% target, that resilience leaves officials room to contemplate another December increase, even as the ECB judges growth risks tilted down and inflation risks up.

Joachim Nagel's Friday speech sharpened the inflation assessment. Energy prices had moved well above September's assumed path, bringing conditions closer to the projections' adverse scenario, the Bundesbank president said. Gas and electricity momentum had strengthened, upstream costs were rising and short-term expectations had followed headline inflation upward. If conditions persisted, further action was highly probable; each additional month of elevated inflation increased the risk of second-round effects.

ECB succession talks acquired a more immediate timetable. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Friday that Berlin would propose a package for three Executive Board vacancies in the coming week, with intensive discussions continuing and agreements unfinished. Candidates for the positions held by Isabel Schnabel and Philip Lane must be submitted by November 18, ahead of recommendations for the November 26-27 leaders' summit. Schnabel leaves in January, Christine Lagarde in February and Lane in May.

Klaas Knot, competing with Pablo Hernandez de Cos for the presidency, used a Sunday interview with Corriere della Sera to set out his position on sovereign support and inflation. ECB intervention can shield markets from disorderly dynamics, he said, while sound fiscal policy remains governments' responsibility. He described resilient domestic demand, employment and private balance sheets, along with defense expenditure and spillovers from U.S. AI investment, as supports for activity.

Knot's inflation emphasis was measured: expectations remained anchored and evidence of broad second-round effects was limited. Whether energy pressure spreads into wages and wider prices remained the key issue, with Middle East developments decisive. That prospective policy stance comes as governments weigh candidates who may have to manage both inflation and renewed sovereign-market turbulence.

Peru delivered a realized policy change Thursday, raising its key rate 25 basis points to 4.50%, its first increase in nearly four years. Most surveyed analysts expected the move; only two of 13 anticipated a hold. October inflation reached 5.25%, the fastest since 2023 and the eighth consecutive month above the 3% target ceiling, as food and energy costs rose.

The central bank expects headline and core inflation to return toward 2% as supply shocks fade, while warning that El Niño and Middle East tensions could prolong them. It explicitly left the next decision open rather than committing to a series of increases. Governor Julio Velarde had raised the 2026 inflation forecast to 4.2% from 3.8% in September, with a return to the target range projected for 2027.

Mexico's policy divergence remained under scrutiny after its surprise cut, with fresh reporting highlighting disagreement about its purpose. Bank of America's Carlos Capistran said investors questioned whether supporting growth through a weaker peso or reducing government financing costs had influenced the decision. Governor Victoria Rodríguez denied targeting a particular currency level and described the recent adjustment as orderly after substantial appreciation. The peso had fallen almost 9% from its early-September high to around 18.60 per dollar, and Bank of America expects 19 next year. These attributed interpretations sit alongside October inflation of 3.75% and Banxico's signal that it is in no hurry to cut again.

## Debt Negotiations and Earnings Reprice Individual Borrowers

Senegal's budget impasse outweighed progress on debt verification. Its 2031 dollar-bond yield rose 109 basis points over the week to the highest since September, while the 2033 yield increased 75 basis points. The government needs parliamentary approval for a revised 2026 budget and the 2027 spending plan underpinning its preliminary $2.2 billion IMF agreement. Lawmakers from Ousmane Sonko's majority Pastef party oppose elements of the adjustment, particularly cuts to public investment; Sonko has also challenged the conditions for the debt restructuring.

The appointment of Deloitte, made last month and disclosed in Friday reporting, advances one required step toward IMF board consideration. An earlier reconciliation by Forvis Mazars had prompted revision of end-2023 central-government debt to 111% of GDP from around 74%; the IMF estimated debt at 132% at end-2024. The dates and differing estimates underline the scale of the accounting problem the new audit must address.

IMF spokeswoman Julie Kozack said Thursday that the budget must be consistent with agreed policies and implementable within Senegal's legal and constitutional framework. Corrective measures for debt misreporting and financing assurances are also required. An official creditor committee including China and France has yet to be formed. Senegal is targeting agreements in principle with official creditors and bondholders by December, with Lazard and Global Sovereign Advisory advising the country and Alvarez & Marsal and White & Case advising a bondholder group.

Venezuela's multilateral financing prospects advanced on a different track. The IDB board agreed Friday to re-engage through a framework for technical assistance, private-sector support and potential investments. Separately, the U.S. Treasury is considering an overnight bridge arrangement to clear roughly $2.3 billion of Venezuelan arrears with the lender, according to people familiar with the discussions. The contemplated funds would go to the IDB rather than directly to Venezuela.

Clearing arrears would allow the IDB to resume lending after its 2018 suspension and enable requests to other multilateral institutions. Potential IDB loans could reach $6 billion over two years, while the World Bank has said it could lend up to $5 billion over that period. Senator Elizabeth Warren has previously opposed use of Treasury's Exchange Stabilization Fund for guarantees to financial firms investing in Venezuela, leaving congressional scrutiny relevant to the proposed financing route.

Corporate earnings produced a sharp, immediate repricing in Brazil. CSN's 2031 dollar notes fell 3.38 cents to 48 cents at 11:06 a.m. New York Friday, according to TRACE data cited by Bloomberg. Shares dropped as much as 12% to their lowest intraday level since 2016. Q3 adjusted net income swung to a 1.25 billion-real loss from a 76 million-real profit a year earlier, while EBITDA fell 43% to 1.88 billion reais, below the 1.94 billion-real analyst estimate.

Higher costs, lower iron-ore prices, weaker overseas steel sales and cement production expenses weighed on results. Net debt stood at 44.9 billion reais and net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 4.23 times. Chief Executive Fabio Schvartsman said the company would seek lower bank rates and maturity extensions after completing pending asset sales. Agreed disposals include the cement unit for 12.7 billion reais and the German steel business at an enterprise value of about €550 million.

CSN is still prioritizing the P15 iron-ore expansion for 2028. Construction is increasing current capital spending, while the company expects the project eventually to add 16.5 million tons of high-grade annual output and more than 4 billion reais of long-term earnings before items. Those prospective benefits leave current cash generation and the execution of asset sales central to deleveraging.

Malaysia's Zetrix AI faces a covenant issue as well as overdue payments. Founder Wong Thean Soon sold 2.22 billion shares between June and October to meet margin calls, losing his position as the largest shareholder and putting the company at risk of breaching Islamic-bond terms requiring him to retain that status. MARC cut its debt rating to one rung above default, and Zetrix disclosed 25 million ringgit of bond payments due November 6 remained owed.

The company is also contending with the suspension of its remaining road-toll collection service after authorities said it owed 314 million ringgit of government fees. Wong said priorities were fulfilling obligations and strengthening operations as Zetrix shifts toward AI, blockchain and international business. Those plans follow a profound loss of its former government-services franchise and a decline in market capitalization to about 430 million ringgit from a 10.5 billion-ringgit peak.

Another fresh secondary-market warning emerged in acquisition finance. A loan exceeding $1 billion for Intersnack's $2.9 billion Utz takeover was indicated near 88 cents this week, against September pricing at 99, before the acquisition's expected close. The marked decline shortly after issuance adds a distinct borrower-level price signal to a day of only modest broad high-yield spread widening.

## Scarce Supply and Local Funding Reshape Demand

Emerging-market sovereign issuance has contracted sharply even as recent transactions attracted substantial orders. Bloomberg's weekend analysis put second-half hard-currency sales at $69 billion, down 41% from the comparable period a year earlier, with issuance since September roughly halved. Pictet's Reza Karim attributed the shortage of viable windows to volatile U.S. rates and geopolitical risk; Promeritum's Chris Celio said the swings made confident book-building difficult.

Recent demand supports that distinction. William Blair's Yvette Babb cited orders around five times Peru's offering and three times Ecopetrol's, while an Indonesian sukuk drew triple coverage and tightened 25-30 basis points from initial guidance. Romania's €4.5 billion transaction received more than €7.6 billion of orders. Cash unable to find new issues can flow toward existing debt, supporting secondary-market prices, Celio said.

The asset class had lost 0.5% this year in Bloomberg's comparison, against losses of 1.5% for Treasuries and 1.8% for U.S. corporate debt. TT International's Jean-Charles Sambor expected continued outperformance specifically against U.S. high yield, citing stronger technicals, lower supply risk and improving fundamentals. Karim anticipated a potentially large revival of issuance early in 2027, making the durability of today's scarcity support dependent on the reopening of funding windows.

India's largest pension manager is preparing for the opposite supply pattern in state debt. SBI Pension Fund, with about $64 billion under management, plans greater incremental purchases as provincial borrowing rises in the January-March quarter. Chief Investment Officer Sandeep Pandey expects the yield premium over federal debt to widen again. The 10-year premium is about 60 basis points after reaching a nearly five-year high of 90 in April.

State bonds represented about 17% of SBI's holdings at end-October. The manager has reduced duration over 18 months and recently increased cash, while focusing on income from state and top-rated corporate debt. Its planned allocation shows how competing public borrowers can redirect institutional demand when federal borrowing is also large.

China's policy-bank market experienced a more immediate allocation shock. China Development Bank's 10-year yield rose 3 basis points Thursday, matching its largest daily increase this year, and its premium over comparable sovereign debt widened to about 9 basis points, the most in more than six months. Export-Import Bank of China and Agricultural Development Bank of China yields also rose.

The new market response followed concern that a potential tax on sovereign interest income would lift government yields and force repricing elsewhere. Huachuang attributed the policy-bank selloff to that concern; Tianfeng said mutual funds could reconsider allocations if higher sovereign yields eroded the relative appeal of policy-bank notes. The levy remains under consideration, with the price adjustment already extending beyond the government securities directly affected by the consultation.

Vietnam's banks are drawing household money away from equities as loan growth outpaces deposit growth. Deposit rates rose for 11 consecutive months before the central bank ordered reductions in late October. Some lenders still offer up to 7% at counters, while customers interviewed by Bloomberg obtained negotiated rates above 9%, mainly from smaller and medium-sized institutions. Kenno Asset Management's Chris Hunt described tight liquidity and strong loan demand as drivers of the competition for funds.

The reallocation is visible in securities accounts, where cash fell 49% annually to 64.9 trillion dong at end-Q3, the lowest since Q4 2024. October equity turnover fell to its weakest monthly level since August 2020. Household deposits reached 11.43 quadrillion dong at end-August, while foreign investors sold a net $4.6 billion of shares this year, close to the full-year 2025 record of $4.8 billion. High bank funding rates are shaping domestic asset demand even after market-access reforms secured Vietnam's FTSE Russell emerging-market upgrade.

Zimbabwe is seeking to build a longer local-currency curve. Governor John Mushayavanhu said the central bank plans to extend its ZiG term-deposit facility beyond existing 30- and 90-day instruments and expects government bonds to follow. The September instruments yielded 8% and 11% and were fully subscribed. The objective is to make the currency a store of value alongside its transactional use.

That ambition follows substantial currency support. The central bank spent $1.35 billion intervening in the first nine months of 2026, while the ZiG weakened almost 3%. Mushayavanhu said reserves above $2 billion could cover the ZiG32 billion in circulation at an implied rate around 18 per dollar, compared with Thursday's 26.43 market rate. His assessment of undervaluation accompanies the planned market development, with the reserve comparison representing the governor's calculation.

Market operations faced an independent disruption Friday as Microsoft's outage delayed communications and trade processing. Singapore traders reported some financing deals could not be completed; European exchanges experienced email problems, and Japanese desks used phones and fax. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura said execution largely continued but confirmations accumulated, creating settlement problems. Kyte Broking's Andy Kent expected reduced willingness to trade until straight-through processing recovered. Microsoft reported progress toward restoring service during the U.S. session.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan separately proposed distinguishing securities bought for market functioning from those held for monetary policy. A separate account with a commitment to sell intervention assets promptly could reduce unintended stimulus, she said Friday. She assesses Treasury functioning through bid-ask spreads, depth and price impact, rather than treating a rapid yield rise alone as sufficient reason to intervene. She also called for institutions to prepare access to emergency liquidity and for designated financial-market utilities to have discount-window access in unusual circumstances, including weekends and holidays.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. data will test how much demand can withstand higher real borrowing costs. November's Empire State manufacturing index is due November 16, with Trading Economics forecasting 10 after 25.5. Weekly ADP employment on November 17 follows a 19,750 reading, and October retail sales are forecast to rise 0.6% after 0.8%. Import prices are forecast up 1.7% monthly after 1.1%, and export prices up 1.4% after 2.2%, adding separate observations of externally transmitted costs.

The Fed's October minutes and forthcoming appearances by Chair Kevin Warsh, Williams and Neel Kashkari will help distinguish support for consecutive quarter-point increases from urgency for a larger step. The minutes record a meeting held before the strong October payroll and CPI reports, when two officials dissented in favor of tightening. Warsh's Monday event concerns AI and productivity, a subject relevant to Jefferson's neutral-rate uncertainty, although he has avoided near-term policy guidance. Treasury's forthcoming 20-year and 10-year inflation-linked sales add tests of duration demand after the weekly selloff.

Initial claims on November 19 are forecast at 194,000 after 200,000, while continuing claims are forecast at 1.725 million after 1.697 million. The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index is projected at 19 after 20.9. Those releases will bring fresh information on labor retention and industrial activity as the rate debate increasingly turns to the persistence of growth alongside inflation.

China's Monday activity release will provide the first broad read after its late-September support measures. Economists expect industrial production growth of 5.3% annually and retail sales of 0.8%, down from September's 1.1%; January-October fixed investment is expected to have declined 1.7%. Policy-bank financing of 800 billion yuan had been deployed by October 28, and local governments received another 250 billion yuan of special-bond quota for investment by year-end. The figures will show how far that financing is translating into activity before December's economic-policy gathering.

Japan's Q3 GDP is forecast to slow to 0.2% annualized from 1.4%, with private consumption potentially contracting. Its October CPI later in the week is expected to move further above the BOJ's 2% goal. These observations bear directly on whether renewed tightening expectations are consistent with domestic demand. Australia's wage and employment releases and RBA minutes will provide separate tests of the relative-rate divergence already visible in Australian and U.S. bonds.

Britain's labor release Tuesday and CPI Wednesday carry particular significance after resilient growth. The headline inflation forecast is 3.6%, driven by fuel and household energy costs. Labor expectations differ: Bloomberg Economics forecasts unemployment of 4.6% in the three months through September, while the broader week-ahead account expects 4.7%. The BOE's assessment of whether energy pressure is spreading will matter for a possible December increase. Canada reports inflation Monday, with headline growth forecast at 3.2% but core measures near 2%; Bank Indonesia's Wednesday decision is expected in early projections to deliver a 25-basis-point increase amid rupiah pressure.

Nvidia's November 17 results will offer the first major operating assessment under interim leadership after shares lost 13% over the week. The company's ability and willingness to continue financing customers remains relevant to Nscale's funding needs and wider chip-backed borrowing. Weekend reporting added pressure for a leadership shakeup and a reported discussion of a possible Huang return, while the company had said it was still selecting a search firm. Anthropic's impending offering will independently test the conversion of strong orders into funding. Dealers expect about $35 billion of U.S. bond sales in the coming week; all respondents in a European survey expect at least €30 billion-equivalent.

Senegal's budget approvals, financing assurances and creditor negotiations remain the steps determining progress toward IMF board consideration. Venezuela's proposed bridge facility has a separate threshold: an agreed mechanism to clear arrears before new multilateral loans can proceed. Neither timetable is resolved by the latest appointments or board framework alone.

Energy security remains an independent source of uncertainty after a weekend escalation. Iran's military said it launched six drones at a Bahrain air base, its first such attack since early September, while reiterating that a route to ending the war remained open. That later development follows Friday's IEA projection of a quarterly oil surplus, the first since the war began. Friday's WTI futures close was $88.56, down 0.20%, while Brent was $95.84, up 0.02%; the effect of the weekend attack remains to be established when markets resume.

overall_summary.headline: Softer PPI lifts short-dated Treasuries as longer yields edge higher
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Short-dated Treasuries recovered Friday after October PPI rose 0.3%, below the 0.4% consensus, easing concern about a half-point Fed increase. The 2-year yield fell 3.95 basis points to 4.8419%, while the 10-year rose 0.81 basis point to 5.1352%; the gap widened 4.76 basis points to 29.33 basis points. Underlying pressure persisted: PPI excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% for a second month, and Fed officials continued to make the case for further restraint while differing over its pace and employment risks.

The daily recovery followed a sharp weekly selloff. The 2-year yield remained 33.04 basis points higher over the week and the 10-year 27.78 basis points higher. Real yields accounted for most of the longer-maturity repricing: the 10-year TIPS yield rose 1.85 basis points Friday to 2.8847%, while the breakeven fell 1.04 basis points to 2.2505%. Markets were pricing around 90 basis points of tightening by September 2027, versus roughly 50 a week earlier.

AI financing showed concrete strains. QTS cut a planned raising to about $300 million from roughly $800 million after pricing resistance and investor exposure limits. Nscale disclosed $5.5 billion of debt and a need for at least $30 billion more to complete its Monarch development, whose Anthropic contract permits termination if funding is not secured or delivery is late. Natixis research identified data-center borrowers' fixed-rate swap payments as an additional source of upward rates pressure. Broad U.S. investment-grade spreads were little changed Friday, while high-yield spreads widened modestly.
